title: Deep learning on diffusion MRI classifies stroke subtype and predicts occult AF
summary: In a prospective diagnostic accuracy study across nine Korean stroke centres, a commercially deployed convolutional neural network classified diffusion-weighted imaging from 617 acute ischaemic stroke patients into modified TOAST categories. Agreement with expert adjudication was 75.7% (Cohen's kappa 0.643), with cardioembolism sensitivity 95.5% and small-vessel occlusion sensitivity 90.6%. Its cardioembolism score predicted newly detected atrial fibrillation with an AUC of 0.722 in 426 patients without prior AF; the authors call this exploratory and in need of confirmation.
ai_technology: Commercially deployed convolutional neural network on DWI classifying TOAST stroke subtype and cardioembolism probability
